query: Write a bash one-liner that prints the ten largest files under the current directory, with their sizes.
result:
```bash
find . -type f -exec du -h {} + | sort -rh | head -n 10
```

This lists each file's disk usage in human-readable units, largest first. It uses `du`, so sizes reflect allocated blocks, which can differ slightly from the apparent file size for small files. If you want exact byte counts, use `find . -type f -printf '%s\t%p\n' | sort -rn | head -n 10`, which relies on GNU `find` (standard on Bluefin/Fedora).
